messages.author: 8a8dac569c928102
messages.subject: ZIP conjugacy and PPOi
parts:
I have used a dZIP for my model for count data, the ZIP was found on this page: https://r-nimble.org/nimbleExamples/zero_inflated_poisson.html

However, I have two questions

Non-informative conjugate prior for p[i] would be dbeta(1,1). However, Nimble does not detect conditional conjugation due to being a self-defined distribution. How can you specify to use the conjugate beta sampler?

Also, I would like to know how to get the likelihood evaluated for each data point, so as to compue PPOi and CPOi. Right now I have

ppo[i] <- exp(zero[i]*(log(p[i])+(1-p[i])*exp(-lambda[i])) + (1-zero[i])*(log(1-p[i])-lambda[i]+count[i]*log(lambda[i])-lfactorial(count[i])))

But this is only applicable for the ZIP case. Is there any other easier way, in order to generalize it for cases as the ZINB or hurdle models without specifying the likelihood?

messages.author: 63cc02caac0434cf
messages.subject: Re: ZIP conjugacy and PPOi
parts:
If by p[i] you mean the zeroProb then, to the best of my knowledge, the beta distribution is not a conjugate prior. This is only true when fitting the zero inflated model with data augmentation https://georgederpa.github.io/teaching/countModels.html . 

To get the likelihood just use the dZIP function. dZIP(x=y,lambda=lambda, zeroProb=p) will give the likelihood for lambda and p when observing y. Although I don't know if this will actually work in the model code, but it will definitely work outside it. You should compute these things after running the MCMC anyway, in my view.

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: ZIP conjugacy and PPOi
parts:
To add a little bit from the perspective of nimble's conjugacy system:

Similar to the "registerDistributions(...)" function, we've also contemplated a "registerConjugacy" function, where you could register additional known conjugate relationships (which could involve user-defined distributions, as in your case) with nimble.  Then, they would be detected and handled automatically, just like other conjugacies.  That said, "registerConjugacy" does not exist, so your other best options are:

(a) Manually adding the conjugate relationship you want to the nimble package.  Start by Forking the nimble repository, and adding a definition of your new conjugate relationship to the beginning of MCMC_conjugacy.R, following the same pattern as the definitions of the other conjugate relationships defined there. Then build the modified package, and load it from an R session.  Using this approach, nimble would then automatically detect this conjugate relationship in models, dynamically generate the appropriate conjugate sampler, and use it in the MCMC.

(b) Otherwise, you could write your own conjugate sampler function, and assign it manually using functions such as conf$addSampler().

Both approaches have merits.

If you choose to go down either (a) or (b), someone could probably help you.

Option (a) might feel daunting, but honestly if you're ok with forking the repository, and building your own local version of the nimble package, then this approach is way easier, in every way.

Cheers,
Daniel
